svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — Fully enclosed, technically
svg.desc: Black-and-white pen-and-ink newspaper cartoon at a windy Wellington bus stop, with wooden villas stacked on a steep hillside behind, trees bent by the wind and leaves blowing past. A fictional bus driver with a cap and moustache leans out of his bus, raises one eyebrow and points to a sign on the door reading Pets: fully enclosed in a carrier, saying: Fully enclosed, mate. Beside the bus a hopeful fictional man in a beanie and flapping rain jacket holds the handle of a small pet carrier that is jammed over the head of an enormous shaggy dog, whose huge body, legs and wind-blown tail stay outside; one floppy ear pokes out of a vent and its tongue pokes through the grille. The man says: He is! Well, the end that gets on first is. In the bus shelter a fictional woman sits with a tiny dog in a carrier on her lap, both looking smug, beside a poster reading Council vote: bigger dogs on buses? Caption: The rules say fully enclosed. The dog says: mostly.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY
THE RULES SAY “FULLY ENCLOSED.” THE DOG SAYS “MOSTLY.”
Source: RNZ Local Democracy Reporting, 23 November 2026 — Wellington regional councillors to vote on whether to relax Metlink’s pet rules.
